correctness.rationale: Each iid-point polygon has exchangeable Dirichlet(1,...,1) normalized circular gaps. The exact first moment uses a Beta(1,n-1) marginal. A Dirichlet(1,1,n-2) pair and the cosine difference identity give all cross-edge products with exact combinatorial factors, producing the exact variance. The finite J_k sum follows by integration by parts. Dirichlet factorial-moment identities yield explicit rational Var(T3) and Cov(T3,T5); Taylor remainder and moment bounds justify all three n-power coefficients. Independent quadrature, exact-rational moment checks, and iid-angle simulations ran successfully, but the analytic derivation is decisive.

originality.rationale: The precise claim is the closed finite-n full-perimeter variance and next two \(n^{-6}\), \(n^{-7}\) corrections; it does not claim the known mean, leading \(40\pi^6/n^5\), central limit theorem, or generic Dirichlet identities. Accessible primary full text of Wang--Li--Xu (2023) gives the same object and moments/CLT but not the evaluated finite variance and corrections; Nikitin--Polevaya gives the mean. Semantic database and web searches found no statement implying the evaluated formula. Bélisle (2011) and Wang--Xu (2018) full texts remain unavailable and historical priority is provisional.
residual_risks: Bélisle (2011) publisher full text inaccessible; abstract establishes the leading CLT but cannot exclude exact finite variance calculations in full text.
Wang--Xu (2018) full text inaccessible; abstract and later citation discuss asymptotics, not an exact finite-n variance; priority not certified.
Nikitin--Polevaya (2020) author-uploaded Russian text rendered imperfectly; its abstract describes means but full appendices cannot be conclusively excluded.

General classical Dirichlet factorial moments can be combined to derive the formulas; the proposed novelty is the explicit evaluated variance and controlled extra coefficients, not the underlying identity.

value.rationale: The perimeter of the iid-circle polygon is an established estimator of circumference, so its finite-sample variance directly measures estimator dispersion. The leading known \(n^{-5}\) scale substantially overstates variance at moderate n; the explicit \(-672\pi^6/n^6\) correction and next mixed \(\pi^6,\pi^8\) term quantify the error. The complete n-dependent second moment is a natural precise invariant and resolves the nontrivial negative cross-edge dependence, without asserting a new CLT.
